hints.title: Second Sale Favorite Brand Verification
hints.text: Determine whether the brand of the second chronologically sold item matches the seller registered favorite brand.

hints.title: Row Number Partitioned by Seller
hints.text: Rank sales per seller ordered by order date. Left join users to rank-two sales and check brand equivalence.

hints.title: Second Item Query Blueprint
hints.text: with Ranked as (select seller_id, item_id, row_number() over (partition by seller_id order by order_date) as rn from Orders) select u.user_id as seller_id, case when i.item_brand = u.favorite_brand then "yes" else "no" end as 2nd_item_fav_brand from Users u left join Ranked r on u.user_id = r.seller_id and r.rn = 2 left join Items i on r.item_id = i.item_id.

hints.title: Complete Implementation
hints.text:
```mysql
WITH Ranked AS (
    SELECT seller_id, item_id,
           ROW_NUMBER() OVER (
               PARTITION BY seller_id
               ORDER BY order_date ASC
           ) AS rn
    FROM Orders
)
SELECT u.user_id AS seller_id,
       CASE 
           WHEN i.item_brand = u.favorite_brand THEN 'yes'
           ELSE 'no'
       END AS 2nd_item_fav_brand
FROM Users u
LEFT JOIN Ranked r
  ON u.user_id = r.seller_id
 AND r.rn = 2
LEFT JOIN Items i
  ON r.item_id = i.item_id;
```

complexity.notes: Window ranking orders by seller and outer joining users runs in linear-logarithmic time.
complexity.whyNaiveFails: Inner joining orders discards users with fewer than two sales, who must be reported as no.
complexity.spaceTimeTradeoff: Left joining users against rank-two order subset cleanly evaluates absence as no.
complexity.interviewerExpectation: Use of ROW_NUMBER() OVER(PARTITION BY seller_id ORDER BY order_date) and LEFT JOIN.

solutions.code:
import pandas as pd

def market_analysis(users: pd.DataFrame, orders: pd.DataFrame, items: pd.DataFrame) -> pd.DataFrame:
    orders_sorted = orders.sort_values(by=['seller_id', 'order_date'])
    orders_sorted['rn'] = orders_sorted.groupby('seller_id').cumcount() + 1
    second_orders = orders_sorted[orders_sorted['rn'] == 2]
    second_items = second_orders.merge(items, on='item_id', how='left')
    merged = users.merge(second_items, left_on='user_id', right_on='seller_id', how='left')
    merged['2nd_item_fav_brand'] = merged.apply(
        lambda r: 'yes' if r['favorite_brand'] == r['item_brand'] else 'no', axis=1
    )
    merged.rename(columns={'user_id': 'seller_id'}, inplace=True)
    return merged[['seller_id', '2nd_item_fav_brand']]
solutions.approach: Pandas Cumcount Rank and Conditional Column Lambda
